maya: quick sync — noticed 95th latency drifting on a handful of high-throughput routes this morning, maybe related to the continuous-batcher heuristic changes we rolled last week
sam: yikes, which routes? any kernels flagged in profiler? :eyes:
maya: /routes/ocr-extract and /routes/completion-stream-high. profiler shows higher kernel-switch time during microbatch assembly, and kv hit rate dropped ~4% for the latter
toni: that matches the alert we muted earlier — we saw queue depth spikes then some extra microbatch assembly time.
rajeev: putting raw numbers: before rollout median assembly_time ~6ms, after ~9ms; 95th went from 82ms -> 110ms on completion-stream-high
lin: kv cache miss increase could be due to prefix fragmentation after the new batching window heuristic. requests are getting split more often.
maya: my hunch: the route-tier token budget target is too aggressive for these routes, causing premature microbatch cutoffs and extra kernel context switches
sam: can you dump a short trace? even a snippet helps.
maya: pasted a trimmed trace:```
[2026-03-18T08:12:02Z] recv req id=abcd route=completion-stream-high tokens=48 prefer_batch=true
[2026-03-18T08:12:02Z] assigned batch_id=312 seq=1 wait=4ms assemble=7ms kernel_switch=14ms start_exec
[2026-03-18T08:12:02Z] recv req id=abce route=completion-stream-high tokens=312 prefer_batch=true
[2026-03-18T08:12:02Z] got batch_id=312 seq=2 wait=2ms assemble=9ms kernel_switch=26ms start_exec
[2026-03-18T08:12:02Z] kv_lookup miss route=completion-stream-high key=prefix-xyz hit=false
```
toni: notice kernel_switch jumps when a large req joins the microbatch — we might be hitting a codepath that forces kernel(s) swap due to sequence length or quantization path mismatch
rajeev: earlier change in the kernel selector added a fastpath for <64 token sequences on amx kernels. If a >256 token request lands in same microbatch, we trigger a slower fallback kernel, causing the timing blip
lin: so the heuristic that groups by token budget needs to be stricter about sequence-length homogeneity, or the selector should try to keep like-lengths together until a timeout
sam: option A: tighten the token-budgeting gate for these routes (lower the dynamic target by 20%). Option B: change microbatcher to prefer sequence-homogeneous batches at the cost of slightly higher wait time for small requests
maya: prefer a mixed approach: reduce dynamic token-budget target for route-tier "high-stream" and enable sequence-homogeneity for that tier only as a canary.
toni: agree. also we should check KV cache eviction thresholds — fragmentation could be increasing misses when we split similar prefixes across different microbatches
rajeev: i can run a synthetic replay tomorrow to measure tradeoffs. want to run two experiments: (1) reduce token_budget_target by 20% for the route-tier, (2) enable length-homogeneous grouping with 30ms max wait
lin: add a metric to track kernel_switch_count per batch and kv_miss_rate per route to the canary dashboard
maya: actionable plan:
- rajeev: run replay + collect kernel_switch_count, kv_miss_rate, p95 latency for both experiments
- sam: prepare rollout flags (ff) for token_budget_target and length_homogeneity for route-tier 'high-stream'
- toni: add dashboard panels and short-run alert if p95 > 130ms after rollout
- lin: instrument microbatcher to emit batch_length_stddev metric (so we can detect heterogeneity)
perf-bot: experiment job queued: replay-id=rp-20260318-09 config=(reduce_budget_20pct) estimated=45m
perf-bot: experiment job queued: replay-id=rp-20260318-10 config=(length_homog_30ms) estimated=50m
maya: thanks — let’s reconvene after replays. if the homogeneous grouping reduces kernel_switch_count without hurting median latency we can roll to more tiers
sam: one more thing — add a guard so when kv_miss_rate rises >2% we auto-fallback to previous batcher over 10s to limit user impact
maya: good call. I'll add that to the rollout notes.
lin: I'll also run a quick fiber profile to see if kernel selection path is allocating unexpectedly
rajeev: starting replay now, will post initial numbers in #eng-runtime in ~1h
maya: done for now. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
